text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API lets your program communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove who you are. Be careful about rate limits, because APIs usually allow only a certain number of requests per minute or hour. Finally, always add error handling to your code. Check status codes and handle failures gracefully, so your application stays reliable even when something goes wrong.
